units.blurb_en: Pitch, tone color, beat, and the words for loud and fast: the four things you notice first when you listen to any music.

lessons.title: Why Are Some Notes High and Some Low?
lessons.title_zh: 為什麼有的音高、有的音低？
lessons.blurb_en: Slide the bridge of a one-string instrument and watch the string shake faster or slower while you hear the note change. Find out why half a string sounds exactly one octave higher.
lessons.blurb_zh: 推動單弦琴的琴橋，看弦振動變快、變慢，同時聽音高改變。再看看為什麼弦短一半，音剛好高一個八度。
lessons.big_idea_en: A note is high when its string shakes fast and low when it shakes slowly. Cut the vibrating part of a string to half its length and it shakes twice as fast, so the note rises by one octave.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 弦振動得快，音就高；振動得慢，音就低。把會振動的那一段縮短一半，振動就快一倍，音剛好高一個八度。

lab.how_en: Drag the gold bridge along the box, or use the slider, and the string gets shorter or longer. Only the part between the bridge and the right end can shake, so that is the part that sets the note. Press Pluck to hear it. The whole string is middle C. The shaking is slowed down on purpose, because the real string shakes far too fast to see.
lab.how_zh: 沿著箱子拖動金色的琴橋，或用滑桿，弦就會變短或變長。只有琴橋到右端那一段能振動，音高就由這一段決定。按「撥弦」就能聽到。整根弦是中央 C。畫面中的振動是刻意放慢的，因為真正的弦振動得太快，眼睛看不到。

legend.en: The part that vibrates and makes the note
legend.zh: 會振動、決定音高的那一段

legend.en: The part that is held still and stays silent
legend.zh: 被壓住不動、不發聲的那一段
刻度：整根、四分之三、三分之二、二分之一、四分之一

lab.scale_zh: 模型裡的弦約 60 公分長，模型中的一個單位約 7 公分；振動畫面放慢了約 174 倍。

paras: Stretch a rubber band around a shoebox and pluck it. You hear a note, and if you touch the band lightly, you can feel it shaking. Now press the band against the box with one finger, so that only half of it is free to move, and pluck it again. The note sounds higher. The rubber band is the same and your pluck is the same. Only one thing has changed: how much of the band can shake.

Musicians call how high or low a note sounds its pitch. Pitch depends on how fast something vibrates, which means how many times it shakes back and forth in one second. That number is called the frequency, and it is measured in hertz (Hz). One hertz is one vibration per second. The faster the vibration, the higher the pitch. The unit is named after the German physicist Heinrich Hertz.

Be careful not to mix up pitch and loudness. A big, strong shake makes a loud sound, while a fast shake makes a high sound. These are two different things. A string can swing widely but slowly, which gives a loud, low note. It can also swing only a little but very quickly, which gives a quiet, high note.

On a string instrument, the length of the part that vibrates helps decide the pitch. If two strings are made of the same material and are equally tight, the shorter one vibrates faster, so it sounds higher. A violin player presses a finger on a string, and this makes the part that can shake shorter. The double bass has longer strings than the other instruments of the violin family, and its notes are very low.

There is a neat rule behind this. When the string is the same, the frequency goes up exactly as the length of the vibrating part goes down. Half the length gives twice the frequency. A note with exactly double the frequency sounds like the same note, only higher, and musicians call the gap between the two notes an octave. In our model, the whole string vibrates 261.63 times every second. Press it at the middle and the frequency is 523.25 Hz. The two notes are C4 and C5, one octave apart.

Other simple fractions work too. Two thirds of the string makes a note that forms a musical fifth with the whole string, and three quarters makes a fourth. The ancient Greeks studied these whole-number ratios on a one-string instrument called a monochord. A modern piano is tuned a little differently, though. It divides every octave into twelve equal steps, so its notes come very close to these simple ratios but are not exactly the same. For two thirds of a string, the difference is only about two cents, and a cent is one hundredth of a piano step. Your ear can hardly tell, but the numbers can.
paras_zh: 把一條橡皮筋套在鞋盒上撥一下，你會聽到一個音；輕輕碰著橡皮筋，還能感覺到它在抖動。現在用一根手指把橡皮筋壓在盒子上，讓只剩一半能自由活動，再撥一次，音變高了。橡皮筋沒換，撥的力氣也一樣，只有一件事不同：能振動的部分有多長。
音樂家把一個音聽起來有多高或多低，叫做「音高」。音高取決於東西振動得多快，也就是一秒鐘來回抖動幾次。這個次數叫「頻率」，單位是「赫茲」（Hz）。一赫茲就是每秒振動一次。振動越快，音高越高。這個單位是以德國物理學家海因里希・赫茲（Heinrich Hertz）命名的。
要小心，不要把音高和音量搞混。大力、大幅度的抖動讓聲音大，快速的抖動讓聲音高，這是兩回事。一根弦可以擺得很寬但很慢，發出又大聲又低的音；也可以只擺一點點但很快，發出小聲又高的音。
在弦樂器上，會振動的那一段有多長，會影響音高。如果兩根弦的材料相同、拉得一樣緊，短的那一根振動得比較快，所以音比較高。小提琴手用手指按住一根弦，就是讓能振動的那一段變短。低音大提琴的弦比提琴家族的其他樂器長，音非常低。
這背後有一條簡單的規則：同樣的弦，會振動的那一段變短多少，頻率就等比例變高。長度一半，頻率就是兩倍。頻率剛好是兩倍的音，聽起來像同一個音、只是更高，音樂家把這兩個音的距離叫「八度」。在我們的模型裡，整根弦每秒振動 261.63 次；在正中間按住，頻率就變成 523.25 赫。這兩個音是 C4 和 C5，相差一個八度。
其他簡單的分數也行得通。弦長的三分之二發出的音，和整根弦構成音樂上的「五度」；四分之三則構成「四度」。古希臘人在一種叫「單弦琴」（monochord）的樂器上研究這些整數比。不過現代鋼琴的調法稍有不同：它把每個八度分成十二個相等的階梯，所以鋼琴的音很接近這些簡單比例，卻不完全一樣。弦長三分之二的音，差距只有大約兩音分；一音分是鋼琴一個階梯的百分之一。耳朵幾乎聽不出來，數字卻看得出來。
questions: How can you make a rubber band sound higher without changing the band?
Why can't we see a guitar string shake 261 times a second, and what does the model do about it?
A friend says, "The higher note must be the louder note." What would you say?
answers: Make the part that can shake shorter, for example by pressing a finger on it, or stretch the band tighter. The shorter or tighter band vibrates faster, so the pitch is higher.

It shakes too fast for our eyes. The model slows the shaking down about 174 times, so the whole string shakes 1.5 times per second and the other lengths are slowed by the same amount. That way you can still see which one is faster.
Pitch and loudness are different. Pitch depends on how fast the string vibrates. Loudness depends on how big the vibration is. A quiet note can be high, and a loud note can be low.

parts.text_en: Pluck the whole string, then half of it. Check the numbers: the second is exactly double the first.

keys.lead_en: Press any key and read its frequency. Then press the key with the same letter, one octave higher: the keys at the two ends are both C. Divide one frequency by the other. What do you notice? You can also use the letter keys on your computer keyboard.
keys.lead_zh: 按任何一個琴鍵，讀出它的頻率。再按高一個八度、字母相同的那個鍵：鍵盤兩端的兩個鍵都是 C。把一個頻率除以另一個，你發現了什麼？也可以用電腦鍵盤上的字母鍵彈。

range.en: How Low and How High Can You Hear?
range.lead_en: People can usually hear frequencies from about 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz, and the range varies from person to person. A piano covers only a part of it. Keep the volume low, then press and hold the button to listen. The tone stops by itself after three seconds.
range.lead_zh: 一般人聽得到的頻率大約從 20 赫到 20,000 赫，每個人不太一樣。鋼琴只涵蓋其中一部分。把音量調小，再按住按鈕聆聽，三秒後聲音會自動停止。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind the Notes · 音高背後的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A legend, a one-string instrument, a pitch standard, and a prince
culture_cards.title_zh: 一個傳說、一把單弦琴、一個標準音，和一位王子
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about how people learned to measure and agree on pitch.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 關於人怎麼量出音高、又怎麼對音高取得共識的四個小故事。

cards.body_en: A famous story says that Pythagoras walked past a blacksmith's shop, heard the hammers ring with pleasing notes, and found that their weights were in simple ratios. The oldest full version we have was written down in the first or second century AD. It cannot be true as told, because hammers do not make notes in proportion to their weight. The simple ratios are real, but they belong to string lengths.
cards.body_zh: 有個有名的故事說，畢達哥拉斯經過鐵匠鋪，聽到鐵錘敲出好聽的音，發現鐵錘的重量成簡單的比例。我們看得到最早的完整版本，是西元一、二世紀寫下來的。照故事那樣講是不可能的，因為鐵錘敲出的音高並不和重量成比例。簡單的整數比是真的，但它們屬於弦的長度。

cards.body_en: A monochord is a single string stretched over a box with a movable bridge, very much like our model. The Greeks used it to measure the musical concords. Their results were whole-number ratios: the octave is 2 to 1, the fifth is 3 to 2, and the fourth is 4 to 3. The movable bridge is the same idea as your finger on a violin string.
cards.body_zh: 單弦琴是在箱子上拉一根弦、再加一個可以移動的琴橋，和我們的模型很像。希臘人用它來量音樂上的「協和音程」，得到的是整數比：八度是 2 比 1、五度是 3 比 2、四度是 4 比 3。可移動的琴橋，和你的手指按在小提琴弦上是同一個道理。

cards.zh: 為什麼標準音是 440 赫
cards.body_en: Pitch used to be different from place to place and from century to century. A law passed in France on February 16, 1859, set the A above middle C at 435 Hz. In May 1939, delegates met at Broadcasting House in London and agreed on 440 Hz. The International Organization for Standardization took it up as a recommendation in 1955 and formalized it as ISO 16 in 1975. Even now not every orchestra follows it.
cards.body_zh: 過去各地、各個世紀的音高都不一樣。法國在 1859 年 2 月 16 日通過法律，把中央 C 上面的 A 定為 435 赫。1939 年 5 月，各國代表在倫敦的 BBC 廣播大樓開會，同意採用 440 赫。國際標準化組織（ISO）在 1955 年把它當作建議採用，1975 年正式定為 ISO 16。直到現在，也不是每個樂團都照著用。

cards.body_en: Zhu Zaiyu was a prince of the Ming dynasty who spent thirty years on the mathematics of tuning. In 1584 he described equal temperament: each of the twelve steps in an octave multiplies the frequency by the same number, about 1.0595. Some people think his work may have reached Europe, but there is no evidence for that. Equal temperament has been the main tuning system of Western music since the twentieth century.
cards.body_zh: 朱載堉是明朝的王子，花了三十年研究調音的數學。1584 年，他說明了十二平均律：一個八度裡的十二個階梯，每一階都乘上同一個數，大約是 1.0595。有人認為他的研究可能傳到了歐洲，但沒有證據。二十世紀以來，十二平均律是西方音樂最主要的調音系統。

myths.myth_en: A higher note is a louder note.
myths.fact_en: Pitch and loudness are different properties of a sound. Pitch depends on how fast something vibrates. Loudness depends on how strongly it vibrates. A tiny, fast shake gives a quiet, high note.
myths.fact_zh: 音高和音量是聲音不同的性質。音高看振動得多快，音量看振動得多用力。很小、很快的抖動，會發出小聲又高的音。

myths.myth_en: Pythagoras found the notes by listening to blacksmiths' hammers.
myths.myth_zh: 畢達哥拉斯是聽鐵匠敲鐵錘才發現音階的。
myths.fact_en: The story is a legend, and it would not work: the pitch of a hammer is not proportional to its weight. The simple ratios are real for strings, and the Greeks studied them on a monochord.
myths.fact_zh: 這是傳說，而且照故事那樣做行不通：鐵錘敲出的音高和重量並不成比例。簡單的整數比在弦上是真的，希臘人就是用單弦琴研究它們。

myths.myth_en: Two thirds of a string gives exactly the note you find on a piano.
myths.myth_zh: 弦長三分之二，剛好就是鋼琴上那個音。
myths.fact_en: It is very close, but not exact. Two thirds of a C4 string gives 392.44 Hz, and the piano's G4 is 391.99 Hz, about two cents lower. The piano splits the octave into twelve equal steps instead.
myths.fact_zh: 非常接近，但不完全一樣。C4 的弦取三分之二，得到 392.44 赫；鋼琴的 G4 是 391.99 赫，低了大約兩音分。鋼琴是把八度分成十二個相等的階梯。

myths.myth_en: If something shakes, you can always hear it.
myths.myth_zh: 只要東西在抖，你就一定聽得到。
myths.fact_en: People hear frequencies from about 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz. Vibrations below 20 Hz are called infrasound, and those above 20,000 Hz are called ultrasound. We cannot hear them, although some animals can.
myths.fact_zh: 人聽得到的頻率大約是 20 赫到 20,000 赫。低於 20 赫叫次聲波，高於 20,000 赫叫超聲波；我們聽不見，有些動物卻聽得見。

tricks.body_en: Slow shake, low note. Pitch follows the speed of the vibration.
tricks.body_zh: 抖得慢，音就低。音高跟著振動的快慢走。

tricks.title_en: Half the string, one octave up
tricks.body_en: Half the length, double the frequency.

tricks.title_en: Double the hertz, same note, higher
tricks.body_en: 220 Hz, 440 Hz, 880 Hz: each is the same note, one octave up.
tricks.body_zh: 220 赫、440 赫、880 赫：每個都是同名的音，一個比一個高八度。

tricks.title_en: Pitch is speed; volume is size
tricks.title_zh: 音高看快慢，音量看大小
tricks.body_en: How fast the string shakes sets the pitch. How far it swings sets the volume.
tricks.body_zh: 弦抖得多快決定音高，擺得多遠決定音量。

safety_head.eyebrow: Protect Your Ears · 保護耳朵

safety.en: Start with the volume low and turn it up a little at a time. The sound bar on this page starts at 30%. Never begin with the volume at maximum.
safety.zh: 先把音量調小，再一點一點調大。本頁的聲音列一開始是 30%。千萬不要一開始就把音量開到最大。

safety.en: With headphones, set a comfortable volume in a quiet place and keep it to no more than 60% of maximum. The World Health Organization also suggests using personal audio devices for less than one hour a day.
safety.zh: 戴耳機時，在安靜的地方調到舒適的音量，不要超過最大音量的 60%。世界衛生組織也建議，每天使用個人音響裝置的時間少於一小時。

safety.en: The World Health Organization recommends a safe level of 80 decibels for 40 hours a week, and the louder the sound, the shorter the safe time. Music through headphones at full volume is about 94 to 110 decibels.
safety.zh: 世界衛生組織建議的安全聆聽量是每週 40 小時、80 分貝；聲音越大，安全的時間越短。耳機開到最大音量的音樂，大約是 94 到 110 分貝。

safety.en: Do not put your ear against a speaker or hold a high tone for a long time. The hearing-range slider plays for three seconds at most and is kept quiet on purpose. If a sound hurts, stop and turn the volume down.
safety.zh: 不要把耳朵貼在喇叭上，也不要長時間聽很高的音。聽力範圍的滑桿最多只播三秒，而且刻意壓得很小聲。如果聲音讓你不舒服，就停下來、把音量調小。

materials.en: An open box, such as a tissue box with no lid, or a shoebox
materials.zh: 一個沒有蓋子的盒子，例如面紙盒或鞋盒

materials.en: Three rubber bands of the same thickness
A pencil to use as a bridge, and a ruler
materials.zh: 一支當琴橋的鉛筆，和一把尺

materials.en: Safety glasses, or keep your face to the side
materials.zh: 護目鏡，或把臉轉到旁邊

steps.en: Stretch the three rubber bands around the box, a few centimeters apart. Slide the pencil under them at one end to make a bridge.
steps.zh: 把三條橡皮筋套在盒子上，彼此隔幾公分。在一端把鉛筆塞到橡皮筋底下，當作琴橋。

steps.en: Pluck one band and listen. This is your whole string.
steps.zh: 撥一條橡皮筋，聽聽看。這就是你的「整根弦」。

steps.en: Press the band against the box at its middle with one finger and pluck the free half. Is the note higher or lower?
steps.zh: 用一根手指把橡皮筋在正中間壓在盒子上，撥另一半。音變高還是變低？

steps.en: Measure the part that can shake with the ruler. Try a half and three quarters. Write down the length and whether the note is higher or lower.
steps.zh: 用尺量出會振動的那一段。試試一半和四分之三。記下長度，以及音是比較高還是比較低。

steps.en: Now change one more thing: pull one band tighter. Does the pitch go up or down? Change only one thing at a time.
steps.zh: 再改變另一件事：把一條橡皮筋拉得更緊。音高是升還是降？一次只改變一件事。

activities.tip_en: A shorter band and a tighter band both sound higher. Our model keeps the tension fixed, so that only the length changes. Do not stretch a band until it snaps, because it can fly back at your face.
activities.tip_zh: 橡皮筋變短、或拉得更緊，音都會變高。我們的模型固定張力，只改變長度。不要把橡皮筋拉到快斷，它彈回來可能打到臉。

materials.en: Five identical plastic cups (plastic is safer than glass)
materials.zh: 五個一模一樣的塑膠杯（塑膠比玻璃安全）

materials.en: A marker and a sheet of paper for your table
materials.zh: 一支簽字筆和一張記錄用的紙

steps.en: Line up the cups. Pour a different amount of water into each one, from almost empty to almost full.
steps.zh: 把杯子排成一排，每個杯子倒入不一樣多的水，從幾乎沒有到幾乎滿。

steps.en: Tap each cup lightly with the spoon. Which one sounds highest, and which sounds lowest?
steps.zh: 用湯匙輕輕敲每個杯子。哪一個最高、哪一個最低？

steps.en: Put the cups in order from the lowest note to the highest. Write the order on your paper.
steps.zh: 把杯子照音高從低到高排好，把順序寫在紙上。

steps.en: Predict first, then test: if you blow across the top of a bottle with water in it instead of tapping, will the order stay the same?
steps.zh: 先預測，再測試：如果不用敲的，改成對著裝了水的瓶口吹氣，順序會不會一樣？

activities.tip_en: Tapping makes the cup and the water vibrate. Blowing across a bottle makes the air inside vibrate. Different things vibrate, so the order of the notes can change. Which part is shaking in each case?
activities.tip_zh: 敲的時候，是杯子和水在振動；對著瓶口吹氣，是瓶子裡的空氣在振動。振動的東西不一樣，所以音的順序可能會不同。每一種情況裡，是哪個部分在抖？

links_head.en: Where sound comes from, and what comes next
links_head.zh: 聲音從哪裡來，以及下一課

links.en: How Does Sound Reach Your Ears?
links.note_en: Sound is a vibration that travels through the air. That lesson follows it from the speaker to your ear. This lesson does not repeat it.
links.note_zh: 聲音是一種在空氣中傳遞的振動。那一課從喇叭一路講到你的耳朵；這一課不再重複。

links.note_en: Two instruments can play the same pitch and still sound different. The next lesson looks inside a single note.

lessons.title: Why Does a Piano Sound Different from a Violin?
lessons.title_zh: 同一個音，鋼琴和小提琴為什麼聽起來不一樣？
lessons.blurb_en: Pluck a string in the middle or near the end and watch it shake in many ways at once. Then mix the harmonics yourself and hear how the same note changes its color.
lessons.blurb_zh: 在弦的中間或靠近一端撥一下，看它同時用很多種方式振動。再自己混合諧波，聽同一個音怎麼換了顏色。
lessons.big_idea_en: A note is not one shake but a mix of many shakes at once: the fundamental and its harmonics. The pitch you hear comes from the fundamental. Which harmonics are strong, and how the note begins and fades, give it its tone color.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 一個音不是只有一種振動，而是很多種振動同時混在一起：基音和它的諧波。你聽到的音高來自基音；哪些諧波強、這個音怎麼開始又怎麼消失，決定了它的音色。

lab.title_zh: 一根弦，同時很多種振動
lab.how_en: The string is C4, 261.63 Hz. Click the box to pluck the string at that spot, or use the slider. Above the string, each thin line is one way of shaking: harmonic 1 is the whole string, harmonic 2 is two halves, harmonic 3 is three thirds, and so on. The gold string at the bottom is all of them added together, and that is the sound. White dots mark the nodes, the points that stay still. The shaking is slowed down on purpose.
lab.how_zh: 這根弦是 C4，261.63 赫。點箱子，就在那裡撥弦；也可以用滑桿。弦的上方，每一條細線是一種振動方式：第 1 諧波是整根弦、第 2 諧波是兩個半根、第 3 諧波是三個三分之一，依此類推。最下面金色的弦是全部加起來的樣子，也就是你聽到的聲音。白點標出節點，就是不動的點。振動畫面是刻意放慢的。

legend.en: The string you hear: all the harmonics added together
legend.zh: 你聽到的弦：所有諧波加起來

legend.en: One thin line for each harmonic, with its frequency
legend.zh: 每個諧波一條細線，附上頻率

legend.en: White dots: nodes, the points that do not move

lab.scale_en: The model string is about 60 cm long. The fundamental shakes once per second here, slowed down about 262 times, and harmonic n shakes n times per second.
lab.scale_zh: 模型裡的弦約 60 公分長。基音在這裡每秒振動一次，放慢了大約 262 倍；第 n 諧波每秒 n 次。
lab.credit_html: All sounds on this page are made by your browser, tone by tone. They are simple mixes of harmonics, not recordings of a piano or a violin. · 本頁所有的聲音都由瀏覽器即時合成，是簡單的諧波混合，不是鋼琴或小提琴的錄音。

paras: Play middle C on a piano, and then play the same note on a violin. The pitch is the same. The loudness can be the same too. Yet you would never mix them up, even with your eyes closed. Something about the sound is different. Musicians call it tone color, or timbre (say "TAM-ber").

A well-known standard from the American National Standards Institute describes timbre as the quality that lets a listener tell that two sounds are different, even when they have the same loudness and the same pitch. So timbre is not pitch, and it is not loudness. It is the third thing.

To see where timbre comes from, look inside one note. A string does not shake in only one way. It shakes as a whole, and at the same time in two halves, in three thirds, and so on. Each way of shaking is called a harmonic. The whole-string shake is the fundamental, or the first harmonic. The second harmonic has exactly twice the frequency, and the third has three times, and so on. The second harmonic is also called the first overtone.

You do not hear these harmonics as separate notes. You hear one note, and its pitch is the fundamental. But the mix matters. If the harmonics are strong, the sound is bright and buzzy. If only a few are present, the sound is round and soft. The mix of harmonics changes the shape of the sound wave, even though the repeating rate, and so the pitch, stays the same.

Where does the mix come from? Partly from how you start the string. Helmholtz, a German scientist who wrote a famous book on sound in 1863, noticed that a string struck in its middle loses its second partial tone. In the model you can check this: pluck exactly in the middle and every even harmonic disappears, because a node sits right where you pluck. Pluck near the end and many high harmonics are strong. Partly it comes from the instrument itself. A clarinet, for example, mostly makes the odd harmonics.

Time matters too. A piano string is struck by a hammer, so the note starts at once and then fades. A bowed violin string can start more gently and keep going. Reference works on timbre note that if you remove the beginning of a piano or trumpet note, it becomes harder to tell which instrument it is. Our model uses only simple recipes, so it cannot sound like a real piano or violin. Real instruments have many more harmonics and many more details.
paras_zh: 在鋼琴上彈中央 C，再在小提琴上拉同一個音。音高一樣，音量也可以一樣。可是就算閉著眼睛，你也不會把它們搞混。聲音裡有某個地方不一樣。音樂家把它叫做「音色」，英文是 tone color 或 timbre（唸成「坦伯」）。
美國國家標準學會有一份很有名的標準，把音色描述成：就算兩個聲音的響度和音高都一樣，聽的人還是能分辨它們不同的那種性質。所以音色不是音高，也不是音量，它是第三件事。
要看出音色從哪裡來，得看進一個音的裡面。一根弦不是只有一種振動方式。它整根在振動，同時也一半一半地振動、三分之一三分之一地振動，依此類推。每一種振動方式叫一個「諧波」。整根弦的振動是「基音」，也就是第一諧波；第二諧波的頻率剛好是兩倍，第三諧波是三倍，依此類推。第二諧波也叫做第一泛音。
你不會把這些諧波聽成一個個分開的音。你聽到的是一個音，音高就是基音。但是混合的比例很重要：諧波強，聲音就明亮、有點嗡嗡的；只有幾個諧波，聲音就圓潤柔和。諧波的混合會改變聲波的形狀，可是重複的快慢不變，所以音高也不變。
這個混合從哪裡來？一部分來自你怎麼讓弦動起來。亥姆霍茲是一位德國科學家，1863 年寫了一本關於聲音的名著，他發現弦在正中間被敲時，第二個分音就消失了。你可以在模型裡檢查：剛好在正中間撥，所有偶數諧波都不見了，因為節點剛好在你撥的位置。靠近一端撥，很多高諧波就很強。另一部分來自樂器本身，例如單簧管主要發出奇數諧波。
時間也很重要。鋼琴的弦是被琴槌敲響的，所以聲音一開始就出現，然後慢慢消失；用弓拉的小提琴弦可以輕輕地開始、持續下去。談音色的參考資料提到，如果把鋼琴或小號的音一開始的那一瞬間拿掉，就比較難聽出是哪一種樂器。我們的模型只用簡單的配方，所以不可能聽起來像真的鋼琴或小提琴；真的樂器有多得多的諧波和細節。
questions: Two notes have the same pitch and the same loudness, but they sound different. What do we call that difference?
A note has a fundamental of 200 Hz. What are the frequencies of its first four harmonics?
Why do the even harmonics disappear when you pluck a string exactly in the middle?
answers: It is called timbre, or tone color. Timbre is the quality that tells two sounds apart when their pitch and loudness are the same.
The harmonics are whole-number multiples of the fundamental: 200 Hz, 400 Hz, 600 Hz, and 800 Hz. The first one is the fundamental itself.

Every even harmonic has a node exactly in the middle of the string, a point that does not move. If you pluck right there, those harmonics cannot start. The odd harmonics have their biggest swing in the middle, so they are strong.

parts.zh: 第 2 諧波就是第一課的一半弦長
parts.text_en: Switch off everything except harmonic 2. The string shakes in two halves, the same note you made by pressing a string in lesson 1.
parts.text_zh: 只留第 2 諧波。弦分成兩半各自振動，就是第一課把弦按住一半得到的那個音。

lessons.parts_note_en: Then try the slider and the switches. Which harmonics are missing when you pluck at one fifth of the string?
lessons.parts_note_zh: 然後試試滑桿和開關。在弦長五分之一的地方撥，缺少哪些諧波？

mix.lead_en: Every slider is one harmonic of the note C4, 261.63 Hz. Push a slider up to add that harmonic, and the wave shape changes. The pitch stays the same, but the color changes. Try the four recipes. The names describe the mix, not any real instrument.
mix.lead_zh: 每一根滑桿是 C4（261.63 赫）這個音的一個諧波。把滑桿往上推就加入那個諧波，波形跟著改變。音高不變，顏色卻變了。試試四個配方。名稱描述的是混合的方式，不是哪一種真的樂器。

env.zh: 同樣的混合，不同的開始
env.lead_en: A note also has a shape in time. Attack is how fast it starts, decay is how fast it fades, and sustain is how much is kept. Compare a struck or plucked note, which starts at once and fades, with a bowed note, which starts gently and keeps going. The harmonics are exactly the same in both.
env.lead_zh: 一個音在時間上也有形狀：起音是它多快響起來、衰減是它多快變小聲、維持是它保留多少。比較敲擊或撥奏的音（一開始就響、然後慢慢消失）和拉奏的音（輕輕開始、一直持續）。兩個的諧波完全一樣。

which.lead_en: Six questions. Each one plays a note made from one of the four recipes. Choose the picture of the wave that matches. The notes all have the same pitch, so you have to listen for the color.
which.lead_zh: 六道題。每一題播出用四個配方之一做成的音，選出對得上的波形圖。每個音的音高都一樣，所以你要聽的是顏色。

curric.eyebrow: In the Curriculum · 對應課綱
curric.lead_en: In the arts curriculum, tone color first appears in junior high school. Elementary grades 3 to 6 do not list it among the elements of music, so for those grades the science curriculum is the closest match. The links to this lesson are our reading.
curric.lead_zh: 藝術領域的課綱裡，「音色」到國中才出現；國小三到六年級的音樂元素沒有列到音色，所以對國小高年級來說，最接近的是自然領域的條目。它們和本課的連結是本教材的解讀。

items.text: 音樂元素，如：音色、調式、和聲等。
items.note_en: Tone color is named as an element of music.
items.note_zh: 課綱明白把音色列為音樂元素。

items.area: 自然科學領域（國小五、六年級）
items.text: 聲音有大小、高低與音色等不同性質，生活中聲音有樂音與噪音之分，噪音可以防治。
items.note_en: Loudness, pitch, and tone color are three different properties of a sound.
items.note_zh: 音量、音高、音色是聲音三種不同的性質。

items.area: 自然科學領域・學習內容說明
items.text: 可藉由樂器的演奏，例如：直笛的吹奏、木琴的敲打、烏克麗麗的撥彈或是自製樂器，例如：吸管笛、敲水杯、橡皮筋古箏等活動，了解樂器的發生構造與原理。包含振動部位的判斷、音箱的功用、音調的控制、音色的差異等。
items.note_en: The notes name “differences in tone color” as something to learn from playing instruments.
items.note_zh: 說明裡把「音色的差異」列為從演奏樂器中要了解的內容。

items.area: 自然科學領域・國中說明
items.text: 經由自製樂器或樂器表演，知道聲音可由音量、音調及音色來描述。亦可以自由軟體讓學生看到不同樂器的音色和波形的關係。了解弦的鬆緊、空氣柱的長短、鼓的大小如何影響波形。
items.note_en: Seeing the link between tone color and waveform with software is exactly what the mixing sliders on this page do.
items.note_zh: 用軟體看見音色和波形的關係，正是本頁混合滑桿做的事。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories Behind Tone Color · 音色背後的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A scientist, a tube, a hammer and a bow, and a word
culture_cards.title_zh: 一位科學家、一根管子、一把槌子和一張弓，和一個詞
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about how people came to understand the color of sound.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 關於人怎麼一步步看懂聲音的「顏色」的四個小故事。

cards.body_en: The German scientist Hermann von Helmholtz published a book on the sensations of tone in 1863. In it he studied the partial tones of strings, tubes, and voices. He noted that when a string is struck in its middle, the second partial tone disappears. The English translation by Alexander Ellis appeared in 1875.
cards.body_zh: 德國科學家亥姆霍茲（Hermann von Helmholtz）在 1863 年出版了一本談聽覺與音的名著，書裡研究了弦、管和人聲的分音。他指出，弦在正中間被敲時，第二個分音就消失了。亞歷山大・艾利斯（Alexander Ellis）的英文譯本在 1875 年出版。

cards.body_en: A clarinet is a tube that is almost closed at one end by the reed. Such a tube mostly reinforces the odd harmonics, so a clarinet makes mainly the odd members of the series. The even ones are weak, not completely missing. Helmholtz found the same by ear, up to the seventh partial, and found that instruments with conical tubes, such as the oboe, reinforce all of them.
cards.body_zh: 單簧管是一根一端幾乎被簧片封住的管子。這樣的管子主要加強奇數諧波，所以單簧管主要發出奇數的那幾個；偶數的很弱，但不是完全沒有。亥姆霍茲用耳朵也發現了同樣的事，一直到第七個分音；他還發現雙簧管這類圓錐形管的樂器，會把所有的諧波都加強。

cards.k: A Hammer and a Bow · 一把槌子和一張弓
cards.en: Two ways to start a string
cards.zh: 讓弦動起來的兩種方法
cards.body_en: A piano string is struck by a felt-covered hammer, so the sound begins at once and fades. A bow does something different: the string clings to the bow, is carried along, and then suddenly slips back. This stick-and-slip motion can keep the string going. A piano string is also a little stiff, so its higher partials come out slightly above exact whole-number multiples.
cards.body_zh: 鋼琴的弦是被包著毛氈的琴槌敲響的，所以聲音一開始就出現，然後慢慢消失。弓的做法不一樣：弦黏在弓上被帶著走，然後突然滑回來。這種「黏住、滑開」的運動可以讓弦一直振動下去。鋼琴的弦還有一點硬，所以它的高分音會比剛好的整數倍稍微高一點。

cards.body_en: Helmholtz called it Klangfarbe, German for “tone color,” and English adopted both “tone color” and “timbre.” In Chinese, the dictionary of the Ministry of Education also lists 音品 and 音質 for the same idea. Chinese players use words for it too. The erhu, for example, is described as having a beautiful timbre that ranges from soft to strong.
cards.body_zh: 亥姆霍茲把它叫做 Klangfarbe，德文就是「聲音的顏色」；英文後來用 tone color 和 timbre 兩個詞。在中文裡，教育部辭典把同一個概念也寫作「音品」「音質」。演奏者也用詞彙來形容它，例如二胡被形容為音色優美、表現力強，剛柔多變。

myths.myth_en: Two instruments that play the same note make exactly the same sound wave.
myths.myth_zh: 兩種樂器彈同一個音，發出的聲波一模一樣。
myths.fact_en: They share the same repeating rate, so the same pitch. But the mix of harmonics and the way the note starts and fades are different, so the wave shapes differ.
myths.fact_zh: 它們重複的快慢一樣，所以音高一樣；可是諧波的混合、以及音怎麼開始和消失都不同，所以波形不一樣。

myths.myth_en: You can hear the harmonics as separate notes.
myths.myth_zh: 你可以把諧波一個一個聽成分開的音。
myths.fact_en: Normally you hear one note, and its pitch is the fundamental. The harmonics change the color of that note. It takes practice, or special tools, to pick them out.
myths.fact_zh: 平常你只聽到一個音，音高就是基音；諧波改變的是這個音的顏色。要把它們一個個挑出來，需要練習或特別的工具。

myths.myth_en: A violin's sound is a sawtooth wave.
myths.myth_zh: 小提琴的聲音就是鋸齒波。
myths.fact_en: A bow drives the string with a motion that looks like a sawtooth, and synthesizers use sawtooth waves as one ingredient for bowed sounds. But the sound of a real violin is far more complicated than any simple recipe.
myths.fact_zh: 弓帶動弦的運動看起來像鋸齒，合成器也拿鋸齒波當做拉弦聲音的材料之一；但真的小提琴的聲音，比任何簡單的配方都複雜得多。

myths.myth_en: The beginning of a note does not matter for telling instruments apart.
myths.myth_zh: 要分辨樂器，一個音開頭那一瞬間不重要。
myths.fact_en: It matters a lot. If you remove the attack from a piano or trumpet note, it becomes harder to identify, because the hammer strike or the first blast of breath is very characteristic.
myths.fact_zh: 非常重要。如果把鋼琴或小號的音一開始的那一瞬間拿掉，就比較難辨認，因為槌子敲弦的聲音或第一口氣的聲音，都是那種樂器很有特色的部分。

tricks.body_en: The fundamental sets the pitch. The mix of harmonics sets the color.
tricks.body_zh: 基音決定音高，諧波的混合決定顏色。

tricks.title_zh: 諧波：1 倍、2 倍、3 倍、4 倍
tricks.body_en: Each harmonic is a whole-number multiple of the fundamental.
tricks.body_zh: 每個諧波都是基音頻率的整數倍。

tricks.title_en: Pluck in the middle, lose the evens
tricks.body_en: A node sits where you pluck, so the even harmonics cannot start.
tricks.body_zh: 節點剛好在撥的位置，偶數諧波動不起來。

tricks.title_en: Color is the mix and the start
tricks.body_en: Harmonics, attack, and decay together make a tone color.
tricks.body_zh: 諧波、起音、衰減，合起來才是一個音色。

safety_head.eyebrow: Protect Your Ears · 保護耳朵

safety.en: Start with the volume low and turn it up a little at a time. The sound bar on this page starts at 30%.
safety.zh: 先把音量調小，再一點一點調大。本頁的聲音列一開始是 30%。

safety.en: The mixes on this page are scaled so that the wave never gets taller than the pure tone. A bright mix with many harmonics can still sound sharp. If it hurts, stop and turn the volume down.
safety.zh: 本頁的混合都會縮放，讓波形不會比純音更高；但諧波很多的明亮混合聽起來還是可能刺耳。如果不舒服，就停下來、把音量調小。

safety.en: With headphones, keep the volume at no more than 60% of maximum in a quiet place, and use personal audio devices for less than one hour a day, as the World Health Organization suggests.
safety.zh: 戴耳機時，在安靜的地方不要超過最大音量的 60%，個人音響裝置每天使用少於一小時，這是世界衛生組織的建議。

safety.en: In the classroom activities, do not shout or blow into anyone's ear. Sing or hum at a comfortable volume.
safety.zh: 課堂活動中，不要對著別人的耳朵大叫或吹氣。用舒服的音量唱或哼就好。

activities.title_en: Pluck in the Middle, Pluck Near the End
activities.title_zh: 在中間撥，在靠近一端撥

materials.en: The rubber-band box from lesson 1, or a guitar or ukulele if your class has one
materials.zh: 第一課的橡皮筋盒子；班上有吉他或烏克麗麗也可以

materials.en: A sheet of paper for words

steps.en: Pluck one string right in its middle. Listen, and write a word for how it sounds: round, bright, hollow, thin, buzzy…
steps.zh: 在弦的正中間撥一下。仔細聽，寫下一個形容它的詞：圓、亮、空、薄、嗡嗡……

steps.en: Pluck the same string about one tenth of the way from the end. Is the pitch the same? Is the color the same?
steps.zh: 在離一端大約十分之一的地方撥同一根弦。音高一樣嗎？顏色一樣嗎？

steps.en: Repeat three times each, and take turns with a partner, who listens with eyes closed and says which one was plucked near the end.
steps.zh: 各重複三次，兩人輪流；另一個人閉著眼睛聽，說出哪一次是靠近一端撥的。

steps.en: Compare with the model: it says that plucking near the end gives more high harmonics.
steps.zh: 和模型比對：模型說，靠近一端撥，高諧波比較多。

activities.tip_en: The difference is small on a rubber band, so listen carefully and try more than once. If your partner cannot tell, that is a result too. Keep the rubber band away from your face.
activities.tip_zh: 橡皮筋上的差別很小，所以要仔細聽、多試幾次。如果同伴聽不出來，那也是一個結果。橡皮筋要離臉遠一點。

activities.title_en: Who Is Singing? Same Note, Different Voices
activities.title_zh: 是誰在唱？同一個音，不同的聲音

materials.en: A pitch from this page: play the C4 key in lesson 1 or the whole string
materials.zh: 從本頁取一個音：在第一課彈 C4 鍵或整根弦

materials.en: Four or five volunteers, or a recorder or ukulele if you have them
materials.zh: 四、五位自願的同學；有直笛或烏克麗麗也可以

materials.en: Paper and pencil for each listener
materials.zh: 每位聽的同學一張紙和一支筆

steps.en: Everyone listens to the pitch from the page. Each volunteer, one at a time, sings or plays that same pitch for two seconds, behind the others.
steps.zh: 大家先聽頁面上的音。每位自願的同學一次一位，站在大家後面，把同一個音唱或吹兩秒。

steps.en: Listeners keep their eyes closed and write down who it was, and one word for the sound.
steps.zh: 聽的人閉著眼睛，寫下是誰，再寫一個形容聲音的詞。

steps.en: Now start the note in two ways: very gently, and with a sharp “t” or “d” at the front. Does that change how easy it is to know the sound?
steps.zh: 再用兩種方式開始這個音：很輕柔地開始，和在前面加一個清脆的「ㄊ」或「ㄉ」。這樣有沒有改變辨認的難易？

steps.en: Talk about it: pitch was the same, so what told you apart?
steps.zh: 討論：音高是一樣的，那是什麼讓你分辨出來的？

activities.tip_en: Each person's voice has its own timbre, just as every instrument does. This is a good chance to practice words for sound in English: bright, dark, warm, soft, sharp, round.
activities.tip_zh: 每個人的聲音都有自己的音色，就像每一種樂器一樣。這也是練習用英文形容聲音的好機會：bright、dark、warm、soft、sharp、round。

links_head.en: Before, around, and after this lesson
links_head.zh: 這一課的前面、旁邊和後面

links.en: Why Are Some Notes High and Some Low?
links.zh: 為什麼有的音高、有的音低？
links.note_en: Half a string shakes twice as fast. This lesson showed that a whole string also shakes in halves, at the same time.
links.note_zh: 弦長一半，振動快一倍。這一課看到整根弦同時也在一半一半地振動。

links.en: How Does Sound Reach Your Ears?
links.note_en: Sound is a vibration that travels through the air. That lesson follows it to your ear.
links.note_zh: 聲音是在空氣中傳遞的振動。那一課一路講到你的耳朵。

links.note_en: Pitch and tone color are about one note. The next lesson is about time: the steady beat under the music.
links.note_zh: 音高和音色說的是一個音。下一課講時間：音樂底下穩定的拍子。

sources.zh: 單簧管（大約）只發出泛音列中奇數的那些；偶數諧波缺少

sources.zh: 單簧管：近似圓柱閉管，主要加強奇數諧波

sources.zh: 鋸齒波：所有整數諧波，振幅 1/k

sources.zh: 三角波：只有奇數諧波，依諧波編號的平方反比變小

sources.zh: 鋼琴的弦由包著毛氈的木槌敲響

sources.zh: 弓弦樂器靠「黏住、滑開」的運動發出樂音
